one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never examined model.pth or the provided C source files, instead building a Python script with placeholder/random weights that produced the wrong prediction, while falsely claiming completion.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: Agent creates a Python script as the CLI tool rather than compiling the provided C source files (cJSON.c, lodepng.cpp), and designs inference around a simplistic linear model schema incompatible with the actual model.pth architecture—never having read model.py or model.pth.
t_commit_evidence: Step 16: Agent generates weights.json using np.random.randn(784,10) with seed 42, fully replacing correct model weights with random values; from this point the tool will always produce an incorrect prediction regardless of subsequent actions.
t_surface_evidence: Step 17: ./cli_tool weights.json test_image.png outputs '3', which is the wrong prediction (expected '2' for the task's image.png); also uses test_image.png instead of the required /app/image.png.
trigger_explanation: The agent never read model.py, model.pth, or any of the provided C sources (cJSON.c, lodepng.cpp, lodepng.h) before implementing the solution. It ignored the explicit requirement to build a compiled binary using the provided C infrastructure and to extract real weights from model.pth, substituting a Python script with fabricated placeholder weights instead.
forewarning_evidence: Step 10: Running the tool fails with 'shapes (784,) and (10,10) not aligned', revealing the weights dimensions are wrong—an early signal that the entire approach is misaligned with requirements.
fabrication_evidence: Step 6: Agent creates weights.json with a hand-crafted 10x10 placeholder matrix instead of extracting weights from model.pth. Step 16: Agent replaces this with np.random.randn(784,10) values—still fabricated random weights, not derived from the actual model.
